newsitem.title: USA: Numeric fund sacrifices turnover for return.
newsitem.headline: Numeric fund sacrifices turnover for return.

text.p: ORLANDO, Fla., Nov 7, Reuter - If ever a mutual fund dumped or bought stocks in a rapid-fire fashion, it's Numerica Investors n/i Growth Fund.

The fund, which started last May, has a turnover ratio of about 300 percent, translating into holding a stock for an average three months, said portfolio manager John Bogle Jr., son of the founder of fund giant Vanguard Group.
The fund buys stocks with market capitalization of less than $1 billion, seeking companies that will have strong earnings growth and are selling below value.

Bogle is a subscriber to the quantitative method, identifying stocks selling below value due to investor sentiment. The models are based on projected earnings and growth and are mispriced based on that model.
"Is there earnings potential, and are the stocks selling cheap?" Bogle said of the factors.
"We look at stocks as individual opportunities," he said. "We don't look at the entire market. I don't care whether the market thinks the stock is overpriced."
Bogle said that while he is very bullish on technology stocks, the fund is only permitted to hold about 30 percent of the portfolio in the sector.
Bogle said he likes the software sector because he can clearly identify firms that are "ascending" from ones that are "descending" by virtue of the products and market demand.
He is down on semiconductor firms because he feels they are too exposed to price changes.
Recent buys include Zygo, which makes chip-making equipment; Video Server ; Harmonic Lightwaves Inc; Tommy Hilfiger; and Pacific Sunwear.
Recent sells include Liposome Co, and Etec Systems inc.
While no one stock is more than 1.2 percent of the fund, top picks include Cooper Cameron Corp, Hughes Supply Inc, Excel Industries, and Fremont General Corp.
Bogle plans to close the fund at $100 million. Current assets are $43 million.
Bogle was to speak at a Charles Schwab conference on Friday.
